(5) A Brief History of OAI & OpenAPI

  • Started out in 2011 as Swagger [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swagger_(software)]
  • Swagger was renamed to OpenAPI at the beginning of 2016
    • Donated to the OpenAPI Initiative (OAI) [https://www.openapis.org/] (part of the Linux Foundation [https://www.linuxfoundation.org/])
    • Swagger [https://swagger.io/tools/open-source/] now refers to tools offered by SmartBear [https://smartbear.com/]
  • OpenAPI has been the official name since 2016
    • OpenAPI 2.0 [https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v2.0.html] was the name after the rename (it's the same as Swagger 2.0)
    • OpenAPI 3.0 [https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.0.4.html] was released in July 2017
    • OpenAPI 3.1 [https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.1.html] was released in February 2021
    • OpenAPI 3.2 [https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.0.html] was released in September 2025

(13) More Tools



APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: OpenAPI Track Welcome

(14) Just Use MCP?

  • The pitch: APIs are old, MCP is the future
  • Wrap anything in MCP → call it AI-ready
  • Skip the hard API work → straight to AI
  • Just start fresh after 10 years of API landscape work?


APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: OpenAPI Track Welcome

(15) Problem 1: Directly Exposing APIs

  • Auto-generate MCP from OpenAPI for every API
  • Context window explosion on real workloads
  • Bad descriptions → bad MCP
  • AI still has to invent workflows across endpoints
  • Now your agents get to have a poor integration experience


APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: OpenAPI Track Welcome

(16) Problem 2: Investing in the MCP Layer

  • Hand-craft MCP servers, design the best tools
  • The investment goes into the MCP layer
  • The capability layer underneath remains untouched
  • Better capabilities benefit everyone, not just MCP
  • Everybody's integration experience should benefit


APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: OpenAPI Track Welcome

(17) MCP-Washing

  • Skip the API work → jump to MCP → call it AI-readiness
  • This is the wrong place to invest from a strategy perspective
  • MCP should be a thin layer, not a fat one
  • Invest in your APIs and then expose them through MCP


APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: OpenAPI Track Welcome

(18) Better Described Tools



APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: OpenAPI Track Welcome

(19) Better Descriptions ⇏ Scalable Tool Use

  • Better AX reduces confusion and misuse
  • But even well-described tools still overload agent context
  • The problem shifts from understanding tools to finding the right ones
  • Next: Dynamic Tool Discovery [Dynamic Tool Discovery (1)]


APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: OpenAPI Track Welcome

(20) Dynamic Tool Discovery



APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: OpenAPI Track Welcome

(21) Dynamic Discovery ⇏ Ideal Tool Landscape

  • Discovery helps reduce tool overload
  • Agents still have to invent workflows from scratch
  • We need higher-level, business-aligned tools
  • Next: Workflow-Based Tools [Workflow-Based Tools (1)]
